examples.description: Executable bounded fixture: declared fastener and method qualifications.

failures.trigger: Substituting fastening methods or moving connected objects.
failures.cause: Method/fastener compatibility and attachment constraints are independent qualifications, as asserted by regression tests.
failures.correction: Preserve method identity; qualify current relationships before every mutation.

lenses: Mechanics: distinguish method, resource allocation and resulting relationship.
Player consequence: recovery can reopen passage without making sight equivalent to movement.

examples.description: Executable noncanonical fixture: rinsing conserves water while relocating residue.

failures.trigger: Rinsing a dry brush into a bath.
failures.cause: Residue transfer must not consume or manufacture water; the named test asserts both quantities.
failures.correction: Track water and residue separately and preserve their conserved totals.

lenses: Ecology/chemistry analogy is a proposal lens, not universal hydrology.
Player consequence: dirty water and recoverable residue persist through transport.

examples.description: Executable bounded fixture: a later failure preserves earlier durable intervals.

failures.trigger: A multi-interval action fails after an earlier committed step.
failures.cause: Acknowledged durable intervals cannot be rolled back as though the entire request were atomic.
failures.correction: Commit and acknowledge intervals separately; retain earlier durable effects on later failure.

lenses: Simulation: separate logical time, environment and ongoing intention owners.
Player consequence: leaving, interruption and return preserve real partial work.

examples.description: Executable installed-terminal reference: help remains read-only.

failures.trigger: Help or observation routes are treated as physical actions.
failures.cause: Presentation requests must not acquire mutation or clock authority; the named test checks time and checkpoint behavior.
failures.correction: Keep help read-only and verify actual installed-terminal behavior.

lenses: Interaction design: offer understandable choices while retaining method distinctions.
Player consequence: asking for help does not spend world time or reveal hidden truth.

examples.description: Executable tooling reference: source changes invalidate a verification result.

failures.trigger: Source changes while checks run, or cached remote data is described as live.
failures.cause: Evidence belongs to its inspected source fingerprint; local cached refs do not establish remote freshness.
failures.correction: Rebuild stale evidence against the actual candidate and report unavailable remote checks.

lenses: Software delivery: executable acceptance is evidence of named checks, not coverage proof.
Human factors: retain a compact task state and resume the first unmet authorized condition.

examples.description: Historical design-scope reference: accepted design does not authorize implementation.

failures.trigger: Treating accepted design, source conversion or fixture behavior as runtime/canon approval.
failures.cause: Design acceptance and implementation authorization are separate dispositions; the named test asserts authorization remains false for that historical tranche.
failures.correction: Read the applicable current owner decision; preserve fixture and source provenance rather than inferring promotion.

lenses: TTRPG/worldbuilding: label repository fact, approved decision, inference and proposal separately.
Cross-domain references suggest questions; meaningful player consequences require approved mechanics and observed execution.
